items.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker: From Prompting to Autonomy – The Evolution of Adversarial AI
items.excerpt: Executive Summary Since the release of our May 2026 report detailing adversarial misuse of artificial intelligence (AI), Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) has observed forward leaning adversaries transition from basic prompting to agentic AI workflows and AI-enabled automation. In these operations, human-in-the-loop latency is dramatically reduced, compressing the traditional window for defenders to respond. In Q2 2026, GTIG observed threat actors compromise a cloud resource, then plan, build, and execute an agent-enabled mass credential harvesting campaign in under six hours. We also tracked UNC6780 using multiple tactics to trick AI coding assistants and large language model (LLM) security scanners into its open source software supply chain compromises. Threat actors are also increasingly targeting AI assets. GTIG observed adversaries with wide-ranging motivations target proprietary AI models and source code, exfiltrate application programming interface (API) credentials, and co-opt victim cloud environments to sustain unauthorized AI workloads. items.title: The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
items.excerpt: Written by: Christopher Romano, Codi Starks, Garrett Mahoney, John Wolfram, Josh Murchie, K Singh, Mathew Potaczek, Mike Lombardi, Rik Dolfing Introduction Mandiant responded to multiple incidents in 2026 in which threat actors hijacked enterprise access to Large Language Models (LLMs), a tactic known as "LLMJacking." Spanning a variety of cloud and LLM providers, these intrusions impacted organizations in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors. Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours. Across individual incidents, we observed fraudulent charges associated with resource consumption exceeding $100,000 USD in a single day, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million USD before access was revoked.
